name: rxrpc-socket
why: socket(AF_RXRPC) (a0=0x21, SOCK_DGRAM, PF_INET) from a non-AFS process is the DirtyFrag RxRPC chokepoint
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for dirtyfrag_rxrpc_behavioral.c's socket(AF_RXRPC, SOCK_DGRAM, PF_INET) record

name: rxrpc-socket-dgram-cloexec
why: AF_RXRPC with SOCK_DGRAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC (a1=0x80002) over PF_INET6 (a2=0xa) from a differently named tool is the same family chokepoint; the socket family must matter, not comm beyond the allowlist. rxrpc_create() rejects any type other than SOCK_DGRAM with -ESOCKTNOSUPPORT (net/rxrpc/af_rxrpc.c:826), so the only successful AF_RXRPC socket is SOCK_DGRAM
source: synthetic: an exploit PoC opening a SOCK_DGRAM|SOCK_CLOEXEC AF_RXRPC socket (the only type the kernel accepts)

name: inet-socket
why: AF_INET (a0=2) TCP socket keeps the socket() surface but is not the rxrpc family; the a0=0x21 family constraint must be load-bearing

name: netlink-socket
why: AF_NETLINK (a0=0x10) socket is the common local-config family; same socket() surface, wrong a0, so it must not fire
source: synthetic: a daemon opening a netlink socket

name: ioctl-on-fd33-not-socket
why: auditd logs socket()'s a0 as the family, but for ioctl() a0 is the fd number; an ioctl on fd 0x21 (33) holds the a0=0x21 atom yet is not the socket() syscall. This is the realistic high-volume look-alike in this schema, so the socket syscall anchor must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: an ordinary ioctl on fd 33 (a0 collides with the AF_RXRPC family value)

name: unrelated-openat
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor
